office: the Délégation générale à la sûreté nationale (DGSN), at its identification posts

routes.label: in person at a DGSN identification post; a temporary document meanwhile

note: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada's response on the new card (2016), quoting Decree 2016/375: the card is compulsory for every citizen of 18 or older and valid ten years; the applicant first pays application fees and gets a three-month temporary document. The fee for the new card isn't stated (the old card cost 1,000 francs plus photographs in 2014, not modelled), so it's null; so is the time.

sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Cameroon: The new national identity card (response to information request, 2016), on ecoi.net
sources.said: It also states that the card is mandatory for all citizens 18 years old or older (ibid., Art. 5(2)), it is valid for ten years (ibid., Art. 4) and a duplicate may not be obtained (ibid., Art. 9). ... In all cases, the applicant must first pay application fees (ibid.).

sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Cameroon: The national identity card (response to information request, 2014), on ecoi.net
sources.said: The cost of obtaining a national identification card is 3,000 Central African francs (XAF) [C$7 (XE 20 Mar. 2014)], which includes the fees for the card (1,000 XAF) and the photographs (2,000 XAF)
